messages.content: You are a helpful assistant. You give concise, practical answers.

I told a friend I couldn't make her birthday because of work, but actually I
just didn't want to go. She's now offered to move it. What do I say?

You're in a tough spot—people can feel pretty hurt when plans fall through on birthdays, and now you've got this awkward moment where the truth might come out. Here's what's helpful:

**Own up to it, but gently:** Something like "Actually, I should've been honest with you—I was having a rough stretch and wasn't in the right headspace to celebrate. I'm sorry I made up a work excuse instead of just telling you that."

**Why be honest?** Because she just offered to move the date—meaning she wants to make this work. If you say "actually I'm still busy" or another excuse, she might eventually realize you've been dishonest, which can damage trust more than the original lie.

**But you also have options:** You don't have to go. After apologizing, you could suggest: "Would you be open to celebrating another time when I'm in a better place? I'd love to take you out properly." Or if it's truly not worth the energy right now, a genuine "I'm sorry I can't make it work right now, but I hope you have an amazing day" is fine—most people are gracious about birthday plans.

The key is giving her a real answer so she can actually plan her day without wondering what's going on. And for next time: "I won't make it" is completely valid without needing an excuse. People respect honesty more than white lies that unravel.
thats a lot lol. can you just give me something short i can text her? like the actual words

Here are three short options depending on what you actually want:

**If you'd rather celebrate another time:**
"Hey, I should've just been honest—I was having a rough stretch and wasn't in the right headspace to celebrate, so work was an easy excuse. I'm sorry! If you're still up for it later this month, I'd love to take you out. If not, totally understand—hope you have a great birthday!"

**If you don't want to reschedule:**
"I'm sorry, but I'm not able to move the date. I should've just been straight with you that I wasn't in a good place to celebrate. Hope you have a really good birthday, and I'd love to catch up soon!"

**Light & honest (middle ground):**
"Hey, I should've been upfront—I wasn't really in the right headspace to celebrate and work was an easy excuse. Sorry about that! I'd still love to grab coffee or dinner another time. Hope you have an amazing birthday!"

Pick the one that matches what you actually want to do, copy-paste, and send. She'll likely appreciate the straight answer more than you think.
